Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Peter Peterson, DOB: Not recorded (35 y/o), Gender: Male, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Dr Jacob (tele-health, Babylon), Practice: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Major Depressive Disorder (provisional) ― persistent low mood, anhedonia, loss of appetite, weight loss, fatigue, ↓ libido (consistent with transcript and DDx)
- Secondary: Situational Anxiety / Possible Panic Episodes (palpitations and breathlessness in elevators; temporal association with job stress)
- Tertiary: Relapsed/undertreated Hypothyroidism (physical comorbidity contributing to fatigue/low mood)

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denied/not reported

Formulation:
Predisposing: Personal history of hypothyroidism; possible genetic vulnerability (family history not elicited).  
Precipitating: Job change 3.5 months ago leading to increased stress.  
Perpetuating: Fatigue, low appetite, decreased activity, marital strain, cessation of levothyroxine.  
Protective: Supportive spouse, intact occupational functioning, willingness to engage in care.  
Current presentation of low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, fatigue and decreased libido is most consistent with Major Depressive Disorder, potentially exacerbated by untreated hypothyroidism and situational stress. Episodic elevator-related palpitations suggest comorbid situational anxiety/panic.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Major Depressive Disorder (provisional)
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Regain normal mood and energy  
  • Restore appetite and weight  
  • Improve marital intimacy and overall quality of life
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Confirm diagnosis (screening tool e.g., PHQ-9; thyroid & routine labs to rule out medical contributors)  
  • Initiate evidence-based treatment (psychoeducation, CBT referral, consider antidepressant after lab review)  
  • Monitor mood, appetite, weight, and risk
- Actions (Patient):
  • Complete ordered blood tests promptly  
  • Track mood, sleep, appetite daily  
  • Engage in scheduled follow-up and recommended therapy sessions  
  • Increase gradual physical activity as tolerated
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Order PHQ-9 and GAD-7 screening questionnaires  
  • Review blood results, including TFTs; reinstate/adjust levothyroxine if indicated  
  • Provide psychoeducation on depression and lifestyle measures  
  • Refer to psychologist for CBT (6–10 sessions)  
  • Consider SSRI if depressive symptoms moderate–severe after medical causes addressed  
  • Schedule review in 4 weeks or sooner if deterioration

Secondary Problem: Situational Anxiety / Possible Panic Episodes
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Reduce elevator-related palpitations/breathlessness  
  • Manage workplace stress effectively
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Clarify anxiety diagnosis (GAD-7, panic screening)  
  • Teach anxiety-management techniques (breathing, grounding)  
- Actions (Patient):
  • Practice breathing/relaxation exercises when using lifts  
  • Note triggers, frequency, duration of episodes
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide brief CBT strategies or refer to psychologist (can combine with depression treatment)  
  • Reassure regarding normal cardiac work-up unless new red-flag symptoms develop

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of depression/anxiety, role of thyroid function, lifestyle measures, red-flag symptoms requiring urgent care
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent low mood, anhedonia, suicidal thoughts, marked weight change, worsening palpitations
- Coping Strategies: Scheduled activity, relaxation techniques, balanced diet, support from spouse, professional therapy

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: To be provided via secure app/email
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Psychologist (CBT) – referral pending
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: 4 weeks (or sooner if labs abnormal or symptoms worsen)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Major Depressive Disorder – High likelihood: Persistent low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, fatigue
- Situational Anxiety/Panic Disorder – Medium likelihood: Palpitations & breathlessness in elevator situations
- Adjustment Disorder – Medium-low likelihood: Symptoms temporally linked to job change but severity suggests MDD

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Exact suicide risk inquiry, sleep pattern, alcohol/substance use, full MSE details, vital signs  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio clear overall; some patient statements fragmented; limited psychosocial detail and no formal risk questioning captured
